terms.meaning: command-line interface, a tool run by typing commands in a terminal
a plain text format that uses symbols such as hash marks for headings
one category of guidance data, such as style, color, or industry

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and usage notes
sections.what: Describes how to call the tool and brings in the core search functions from the same folder.
sections.why: Lets this front end reuse the search engine instead of repeating its logic.
sections.watch_out: Moving this file without its sibling core file will break it.

sections.name: format_output
sections.title: Formatting results for reading
sections.what: Turns a search result into headed, bulleted text that shows the domain, query, source file, and count. Shows a single error line when the search failed, and cuts any value longer than 300 characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the output short and readable, which matters when Claude reads it.
sections.watch_out: Long values are cut off mid-text, so important details beyond 300 characters will not appear.

sections.name: generate_design_brief
sections.title: Builds the printed logo design brief
sections.what: When design brief mode is on, runs a search across the knowledge files and turns the top results into a plain text report. The report has boxed headings and sections for industry advice, style ideas and color palettes, with the brand name in the title when one is given.
sections.why: Likely reason: the brief combines several kinds of guidance into one readable document. Reason for the fixed two-result limit not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The sections are filled only when the results contain the keys industry, style and color, which come from `search_all` and are not shown in the sections given, so a renamed key would silently drop that part of the brief.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command line options and how they run
sections.what: Reads what the user types after the script name: a search phrase, an optional domain, a result count, JSON output, design brief mode and a brand name. It then runs either the brief or a normal search and prints the result.
sections.why: Lets the search run from a terminal without editing code. Each option has help text so the user can see what it does.
sections.watch_out: When design brief mode is on, the `--domain`, `--max-results` and `--json` options are ignored without any warning.

summary: Command-line front end for the logo search engine that prints matches as readable, trimmed text.
purpose: Lets a user or Claude look up logo guidance from the terminal in a compact form.
why: Likely reason: output is trimmed so it uses fewer tokens when Claude reads it.
how: Reads the query and options, runs the search through the core engine, and formats each result. Only the first two sections are visible in this packet, so the rest of the file, including the design brief function and the program start, is not reviewed.
inputs: A query text, optional domain, maximum result count, and a design brief option with a brand name, as described in the usage line.
outputs: Markdown-style text printed to the screen.
risks: Only part of the file is in the packet, so its full behavior is unknown. Values longer than 300 characters are cut off. It depends on the core module being importable.
debug: Run with a simple query and confirm the core module sits next to this file. Check the data files exist. If text looks cut off, that is the 300-character limit.
